open_points.subject: sandbox.execute_function scratch-limit outcome
open_points.text: “Only that error is a scratch hit: a write that fails because host storage is exhausted is an ordinary raised error”
open_points.question: How does the sandbox determine that a write error seen and possibly caught inside agent code was caused by the per-file limit, rather than host-storage exhaustion or another I/O failure, and does a caught limit error still force `resource_exhausted`?
options: Any occurrence of the limit-specific write error forces `resource_exhausted`, even if code catches it; the runner must receive an out-of-band indication
Only a limit error that escapes `run` counts; if code catches it and returns valid outputs, the execution succeeds
Classification uses the exception or errno that ultimately escapes, so caught errors are unobservable
open_points.default_guess: Treat any observed `EFBIG` caused by the configured file-size limit as a scratch hit and return `resource_exhausted` even when user code catches it, requiring the runner to report the hit out of band.
